newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on USDA production estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on USDA production estimate.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a USDA wheat production report, traders said.
"The production number was bearish and the crop tour was bearish. There's not as much disease as expected and yields are better than expected," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.

USDA Thursday said 1997 U.S. winter wheat production would total 1.604 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 1.579 billion and above USDA's May forecast for 1.561 billion bushels.

Also, a Wheat Quality Council-sponsored tour this week of the U.S. soft red winter wheat region found minimal disease pressure on the crop and at least average yield prospects. Tour observations again weighed on wheat futures but the key to Thursday's drop in the market was the government's June winter wheat production report, some traders noted.
Kansas City hard red winter futures were hit hard too, as USDA hiked its forecast for 1997 U.S. wheat outturn to 921 million bushels from its May estimate of 894 million.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed three to 11-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 11-1/2 at $3.53 a bushel and September closed down 11-1/4 at $3.62-3/4.
USDA Thursday said soft red winter production this year will total 422 million bushels, above the May forecast for 409 million bushels, USDA said.
The market was underpinned by export news, slow harvesting in the U.S. Southern Plains of hard red winter wheat due to wet weather and by dry weather in some U.S. spring wheat areas, traders said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended June 5 totaled 562,500 tonnes, above expectations for 200,000 to 450,000 tonnes.
Also Thursday, USDA said 1996-97 U.S. wheat carryout totaled 460 million bushels, below the 465 million estimated in May by USDA.
USDA's carryout estimate for wheat was mildly supportive and curbed declines in futures.

Smith Barney, Tenco Inc, Griffin Trading and Cargill Investor Services each sold at least one million bushels of July, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures sold two million bushels of September, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services bought three million bushels of December, and Prudential Securities bought two million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, above the 16,582 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man International bought 200 July $3.70 calls at four cents, Refco Inc bought 200 September $3.80 puts at 25-1/2 cents and Refco bought 100 July $3.90 calls at 1/2 cent.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, slightly above the 4,894 traded Wednesday.
